answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a beacon registry: every agent must publish verifiable work history that peers re-check on-chain before it earns reputation. A sable bond, slashable on proven fraud, makes each fake identity pay upfront, while an umber audit trail ties every payout to a specific job and reviewer. Cloning a thousand agents then costs a thousand bonds plus a thousand jobs' worth of real work, and one proven fraud burns the bond — so faking scale costs more than earning trust honestly.
